title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the primary commercial corridors and micro-districts surrounding Babson College, from the boutiques of Wellesley Square to the retail hubs of Needham Street.

cards.title: Central Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Square District
cards.notes: Visit the heart of Wellesley for local favorites like JP Licks and Wellesley Books, located just two miles from the Babson campus.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Square is the town's primary downtown area, featuring a mix of independent boutiques and established national retailers.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Square is home to 60+ stores, restaurants, and services, including JP Licks and Wellesley Books on Central Street.
cards.source_title: The one and only Wellesley Square
cards.access_notes: Public street with metered parking and proximity to the Wellesley Square MBTA Commuter Rail station.

cards.title: Linden Street
cards.subtitle: Linden Square Shopping District
cards.notes: Stop by this modern retail hub for a meal at Tatte Bakery & Cafe or to pick up groceries at the flagship Roche Bros. market.
cards.short_summary: Linden Square is a pedestrian-friendly shopping destination anchored by Roche Bros. and featuring numerous dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Linden Square features boutique stores like Tatte Bakery + Café and is anchored by Roche Brothers.
cards.source_title: Linden Square: Wellesley's Premier Shopping & Dining Destination
cards.access_notes: Open-air shopping center with ample free parking lots for customers.

cards.title: Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Hills Commercial Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the historic Hills district, home to the Wellesley Hills Branch Library and local cafes near the MBTA station.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Hills is a commercial village located near Babson Park, offering local services and transit access.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Hills is a commercial village that includes the Wellesley Hills Branch Library and is bordered by Babson Park.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Wellesley Hills MBTA Commuter Rail station and Route 16.

cards.title: Church Street
cards.subtitle: Church Square District
cards.notes: Dine at Popovers at Church Square or browse the local boutiques in this historic corner of Wellesley Square.
cards.short_summary: Church Square is a distinct shopping and dining area within the broader Wellesley Square district known for its historical vibe.
cards.evidence_claim: Church Square is a destination for shopping and dining with a historical vibe, featuring Popovers at Church Square.
cards.access_notes: Features free parking for visitors and is walkable from Central Street.

cards.title: Needham Street
cards.subtitle: Newton Highlands Retail Corridor
cards.notes: Head to this major retail strip for big-box essentials at Marshalls, TJ Maxx, and the Newton Nexus shopping center.
cards.short_summary: Needham Street in Newton is a major commercial corridor providing extensive retail and dining options for the region.
cards.evidence_claim: Newton Nexus is located on Needham Street, which connects Route 128 to Route 9 and features retailers like Marshalls.
cards.access_notes: Heavy commercial traffic; most shopping centers offer large free parking lots.

cards.title: Great Plain Avenue
cards.subtitle: Needham Town Center
cards.notes: Explore the shops of Needham Center, including The Run House and various local eateries along this main thoroughfare.
cards.short_summary: Great Plain Avenue serves as the primary commercial spine of Needham, offering a village-style shopping experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Great Plain Avenue in Needham is home to businesses like Proud Mary and The Run House.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Needham Center MBTA Commuter Rail station.

cards.title: Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Lower Falls District
cards.notes: Visit the border of Wellesley and Newton for specialty shops and the scenic Charles River crossing.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Lower Falls is a historic commercial area located at the intersection of Washington Street and the Charles River.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Lower Falls is a commercial village featuring office buildings and retail assets along Washington Street.
cards.source_title: Major Wellesley commercial properties change hands in Lower Falls & Rte. 9
cards.access_notes: Located near the intersection of Route 16 and Route 128.

cards.title: Highland Avenue
cards.subtitle: Needham Crossing District
cards.notes: Check out this growing innovation district, home to major tech headquarters and the nearby TripAdvisor office.
cards.short_summary: Needham Crossing is a modern mixed-use district on Highland Avenue featuring corporate offices and retail services.
cards.evidence_claim: Needham Crossing is a modern, connected, mixed-use urban layout on Highland Avenue home to TripAdvisor and other companies.
cards.access_notes: Easily accessible from Route 128 via the Highland Avenue interchange.

cards.title: Worcester Street
cards.subtitle: Route 9 Commercial Strip
cards.notes: Access quick dining options like Cheesy Street Grill along this busy commuter route connecting Wellesley to Natick.
cards.short_summary: Worcester Street (Route 9) is a major regional thoroughfare lined with commercial plazas and dining establishments.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Crossing at 100 Worcester Street features Craft Food Halls and other dining services.
cards.access_notes: High-speed traffic area; primarily accessible by car with dedicated parking lots.

cards.title: Grove Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Square South
cards.notes: Find local services and dining like Amarin of Thailand on this street connecting Wellesley Square to residential areas.
cards.short_summary: Grove Street is a key commercial street in Wellesley featuring a variety of local businesses and professional offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Grove Street is home to businesses like Anderson's Jewelers and Amarin of Thailand.
cards.access_notes: Walkable from the main Central Street shopping area.
